newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Fire burns homes, forests near Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Fire burns homes, forests near Jerusalem.

text.p: A forest fire raced through the foothills of Jerusalem on Friday, burning about 40 homes and large tracts of trees but causing no serious injuries before it was brought under control by nightfall.
Flames whipped by high winds came within 100 metres (yards) of the main Tel Aviv-Jerusalem highway on an extremely dry and hot day.
Police spokesman Shmuel Ben-Ruby said three people were hurt when two cars collided head-on in heavy smoke and 13 others were treated for smoke inhalation.
Helicopters and planes dropped water on the blaze. Dozens of fire engines and ambulances were called to the scene, about eight kilometres (five miles) west of Jerusalem.
Police ordered the evacuation of three agricultural villages, Kiryat Anavim, Maale Hahamisha and Beit Nakofa, and parts of the Jerusalem suburb of Mevasseret Zion after the blaze broke out at midday.
Ben-Ruby said some 40 homes were destroyed in Kiryat Anavim and Beit Nakofa, correcting earlier information that houses were damaged in Maale Hahamish.
Israel Radio reported the fire burnt 200 hectares (500 acres) of trees.
The blaze apparently resulted from a rubbish-burning fire which residents of the Arab village of Abu Ghosh had set at a local garbage dump, Ben-Ruby said.
"Such incinerations at the dump are carried out frequently...but there was a strong wind and the fire spread," he said.
A little more than a year ago, a fire devastated pine forests along the western approaches to the city.
